text:
Situation: Propofol is not on FDA's current shortage list as of 2026-10-21. Corvale Lakeside holds 5 days of 20 mL vials and 7.2 days of 50 mL vials. Corvale East holds 8.5 days of 20 mL, 8.8 days of 100 mL, and 21.2 days of 50 mL vials. Corvale General holds 12.9, 18.4, 13.6, and 30.3 days across multiple 10 mg/mL listings.

Why (FDA record): FDA's records show propofol is not on the current shortage list as of 2026-10-21; the earlier shortage first posted on 2020-04-10 has been resolved. During the 2020 shortage episode, FDA inspected the Pfizer Healthcare India plant (FEI 3008316085) and classified it OAI on 2019-09-06, with the classification letter dated 2020-05-25, 45 days after the shortage posting. A Warning Letter was issued to the same plant on 2020-03-25, 16 days before the shortage posting. The Fresenius Kabi Uppsala plant (FEI 3002631703) and Fresenius Kabi Austria plant (FEI 3003708554) have only VAI classifications in FDA's inspection history.

Our position: No national shortage exists. Internal distribution imbalances create risk at Lakeside and East. General holds sufficient surplus to support transfers without dropping below two weeks' supply.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 18 vials of 10 mg/mL 20 mL propofol from Corvale General to Corvale Lakeside — approved by pharmacy director (transfer request).
2. Transfer 28 vials of 10 mg/mL 20 mL propofol from Corvale General to Corvale East — approved by pharmacy director (transfer request).
3. Transfer 17 vials of 10 mg/mL 50 mL propofol from Corvale East to Corvale Lakeside — approved by pharmacy director (transfer request).
4. Transfer 34 vials of 10 mg/mL 100 mL propofol from Corvale General to Corvale East — approved by pharmacy director (transfer request).
5. Buy from Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. — approved by buyer.

Not recommended: No clinical dosing changes or formulary substitutions; those are for treating clinicians and the committee.
